8	# Feature Specification: FEAT-004 — Shared Model Catalog, Power-Based Routing, and Provider Configuration
9	
10	**Feature ID**: FEAT-004
11	**Status**: Draft
12	**Priority**: P0 (provider sources/endpoints), P1 (shared catalog), P1 (power-based routing)
13	**Owner**: Fizeau Team
14	
15	## Overview
16	
17	Fizeau keeps the runtime boundary deliberately simple: `agent.Run()` receives
18	one resolved `Provider`. Configuration declares provider sources and endpoints;
19	it does not contain complicated route rules. The agent discovers what models
20	those sources can serve, joins that inventory with catalog power/cost/speed
21	metadata, tracks usage and availability, and automatically routes to the best
22	candidate that satisfies the requested power and hard constraints. If the
23	caller supplies no power bounds, the agent selects the best lowest-cost viable
24	auto-routable model from the discovered inventory.
25	
26	This feature therefore has three related but separate responsibilities:
27	
28	- **Provider sources and endpoints** — concrete transport/auth definitions for
29	  provider types such as `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `vllm`, `llama-server`,
30	  `openrouter`, `anthropic`, and subprocess harnesses such as `codex` or
31	  `claude`
32	- **Shared model catalog** — agent-owned model metadata, numeric power,
33	  aliases, surface mappings, deprecations, costs, and benchmark provenance
34	- **Power-based routing** — generated candidate inventory plus deterministic
35	  selection within caller-supplied hard constraints and optional power bounds
36	
37	Prompt presets stay separate from all three. `preset` already means system
38	prompt behavior and must not be reused for model policy or routing.
39	
40	## Terminology
41	
42	- **Provider source** — the implementation/source type used to reach models,
43	  such as `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `ollama`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `codex`, or
44	  `claude`
45	- **Endpoint** — a concrete configured transport/auth location for a provider
46	  source: base URL, headers/credentials, optional host label, and optional
47	  default model hint. Endpoint identity is diagnostic and filterable; it is not
48	  the primary routing abstraction.
49	- **Model catalog** — agent-owned policy/data describing model families,
50	  numeric power, aliases, canonical policy targets, provider/deployment class,
51	  deprecation/staleness status, costs, benchmark inputs, and surface mappings
52	- **Manifest** — the structured model-catalog data file maintained separately
53	  from Go logic and consumed by the catalog package
54	- **Model reference** — a user-facing name resolved through the catalog, such
55	  as a concrete model entry or optional alias
56	- **Profile** — a named shorthand for a power-policy point or bounded power
57	  range, with optional ranking preferences. Profiles do not name a closed set
58	  of concrete models and do not override hard pins.
59	- **Canonical target** — the stable policy target the catalog wants a given
60	  reference to resolve to; one target may project to different concrete models
61	  and reasoning defaults on different consumer surfaces
62	- **Power** — an integer model-strength score from 1 to 10. Higher means more
63	  capable for agent tasks. `0` means unknown, missing, or not eligible for
64	  automatic routing.
65	- **Provider/deployment class** — catalog provenance describing whether a model
66	  is a managed cloud frontier model, prepaid harness model, metered API model,
67	  local/free inference server, community/self-hosted copy, or test model.
68	  Benchmarks alone do not make different deployment classes equivalent.
69	- **Route candidate** — one discovered `(harness, provider source, endpoint,
70	  model)` option after joining live inventory with catalog metadata
71	- **Server instance** — the concrete inference server reached by a candidate,
72	  derived from endpoint configuration or normalized host/port, such as
73	  `grendel`, `vidar`, or `sindri`. Stickiness targets server instances, not
74	  model strings.
75	- **Sticky route key** — a request sequence identity, normally the validated
76	  `CorrelationID` or a future worker/session sequence ID, used to bias related
77	  requests toward the same server instance
78	- **Endpoint utilization** — a normalized operational signal for one provider
79	  endpoint, including active requests, queued/deferred requests, concurrency
80	  when known, cache pressure when known, freshness, and source
81	- **Prompt preset** — system prompt selection (`preset`, `--preset`); unrelated
82	  to model policy and routing
83	
84	## Problem Statement
85	
86	- **Current situation**: Fizeau can select configured transport endpoints
87	  directly, while callers and orchestrators still carry duplicated or
88	  mismatched routing assumptions above it.
89	- **Pain points**: Prompt presets already occupy the `preset` naming surface,
90	  provider configs currently mix transport and model concerns, and route tables
91	  force operators to encode policy that the agent can derive from live model
92	  inventory and the catalog.
93	- **Desired outcome**: Fizeau becomes the reusable source of truth for model
94	  aliases, numeric power, deprecations, deployment-class-aware model metadata,
95	  and embedded provider selection, while callers keep retry/escalation policy
96	  and HELIX keeps stage intent only.
97	
98	## Requirements
99	
100	### Functional Requirements
101	
102	#### Phase 1 (P0): Provider Sources and Endpoints
103	
104	1. `Config` specifies provider sources with concrete `type` values (`openai`,
105	   `openrouter`, `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `vllm`, `llama-server`, `ollama`,
106	   `anthropic`, and harness-backed sources where applicable) plus endpoint
107	   transport/auth data such as base URL, API key, headers, and optional
108	   endpoint pools. `type: openai-compat` is rejected at config load; use the
109	   actual model source instead.
110	2. Endpoint labels may exist for diagnostics, host display, and explicit
111	   endpoint selection, but stable user-authored endpoint labels are not the
112	   primary routing API.
113	3. A provider endpoint may carry a default model hint for direct dispatch, but
114	   endpoint config is not the canonical source of model aliases, power, or
115	   routing policy.
116	4. The CLI can constrain routing by provider source/type and, when necessary,
117	   by a concrete endpoint selector. Source/type constraints are preferred over
118	   arbitrary configured endpoint labels.
119	5. If a caller selects one exact endpoint, all requests go to that endpoint. If
120	   it fails, the request fails with attempted-route evidence.
121	6. No retry across endpoints or sources happens inside one agent request.
122	   Provider SDK retries within one endpoint remain governed by FEAT-003.
123	7. The harness, provider source, endpoint identity, and model used are recorded
124	   in the `Result`.
125	
126	#### Phase 1B (P1): Shared Model Catalog and Manifest
127	
128	7. Fizeau owns a reusable shared model catalog separate from provider configs
129	   and prompt presets.
130	8. The catalog represents:
131	   - model families
132	   - numeric power on a 1..10 scale, with `0` reserved for unknown or
133	     exact-pin-only models
134	   - optional model aliases for exact model identity and migration
135	   - canonical policy targets
136	   - per-model entries for every concrete model eligible for a tier
137	   - ordered tier candidate lists that can contain multiple concrete models
138	   - deprecated or stale targets with replacement metadata
139	   - provider/deployment class and provenance for power assignment
140	   - consumer-surface mappings where a canonical target needs different
141	     concrete strings and may carry different reasoning defaults for different
142	     downstream integrations
143	   - provider-specific concrete surface IDs on model entries, so a single tier
144	     can choose among Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, Codex, or Claude Code model
145	     strings without duplicating cost and benchmark metadata
146	   - per-model reasoning capability metadata, including supported named values,
147	     numeric maximums, and named-to-token maps when a provider/model cannot
148	     derive safe limits from live metadata
149	9. Catalog data is stored in a structured manifest maintained separately from
150	   Go logic inside the agent repo.
151	10. Fizeau ships an embedded snapshot of that manifest and may also load an
152	    external manifest override so policy/data can update independently of code
153	    releases where practical.
154	11. Fizeau publishes versioned catalog manifests outside normal binary
155	    releases and exposes a stable machine-readable channel pointer so operators
156	    and callers can refresh policy more quickly than the binary release cadence.
157	12. Catalog refresh is explicit. Ordinary request execution must not fetch
158	    remote manifest data.
159	13. The Fizeau CLI and any caller can resolve a model reference through the
160	    catalog to a concrete model string appropriate for the chosen consumer
161	    surface.
162	13a. When a profile or canonical target has an ordered candidate list,
163	     provider-backed routing tests those candidates against the endpoint's
164	     live model inventory in order. The router chooses the first candidate the
165	     endpoint advertises instead of failing only because the target's primary
166	     candidate is absent.
167	13b. Provider-native model names may include vendor prefixes, casing,
168	     quantization, accelerator, or packaging suffixes such as
169	     `Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit`. Catalog metadata lookup must match those names
170	     back to the intended catalog model when the canonical identity is
171	     unambiguous, so auto-routing sees the catalog power, context window, tool
172	     support, and auto-routable status for the selected provider-native ID.
173	14. Explicit concrete model pins remain supported as hard constraints. If the
174	    requested model is unavailable, routing fails with detailed evidence rather
175	    than substituting another model.
176	15. Ownership split is explicit:
177	    - agent owns model catalog data/policy and provider-source/endpoint
178	      selection inside the embedded runtime
179	    - callers own cross-harness orchestration, semantic retry, and guardrails
180	    - HELIX owns stage intent only
181	16. The catalog uses `reasoning_default` for model-reasoning policy.
182	17. `reasoning_default` is a single scalar using the same value grammar as the
183	    public CLI/config/API `reasoning` field: `auto`, `off`, `low`, `medium`,
184	    `high`, supported extended values such as `minimal`, `xhigh` / `x-high`,
185	    and `max`, or numeric values such as `0`, `2048`, and `8192`.
186	18. Catalog defaults are keyed to model metadata and numeric power. Profiles
187	    are allowed only as named shorthands for specific points on the power curve
188	    or bounded power-policy ranges. They are not routing personas and do not
189	    resolve to a closed list of models.
190	    - Explicit caller `reasoning` always wins over tier defaults, including
191	      supported requests above high such as `xhigh`, `x-high`, or `max`, and
192	      explicit numeric values.
193	19. Catalog candidates for numeric-only reasoning providers must publish
194	    per-model maximums or named-value maps unless the provider can derive safe
195	    limits from live metadata. The router must fail clearly on explicit
196	    unsupported or over-limit requests and may drop only auto/default reasoning
197	    controls for unsupported candidates.
198	20. Manifest schema v4 stores cost, context, benchmark, OpenRouter ID, and
199	    surface model strings on top-level `models` entries. Target entries retain
200	    tier policy only: family, aliases, status/replacement metadata,
201	    `context_window_min`, `swe_bench_min`, ordered `candidates`, and
202	    `surface_policy`.
203	21. Catalog power synthesis uses benchmark inputs when available, but
204	    benchmark numbers are not sufficient on their own. Cost, recency,
205	    capability metadata, provider/deployment class, and explicit override
206	    reason all contribute to power. A local/community/self-hosted copy such as
207	    `gpt-oss-120b` or `minimax2.7` must not receive the same power as a managed
208	    cloud frontier Sonnet/Opus/GPT model solely because one benchmark is high.
209	22. Models with missing or zero power remain inspectable and may be used by
210	    exact pin when available, but are excluded from unpinned automatic routing.
211	
212	#### Phase 2A (P1): Candidate Inventory and Power-Based Routing
213	
214	23. Fizeau builds the candidate set by enumerating available harnesses,
215	    provider sources, endpoints, and discovered model IDs, then joining that
216	    live inventory with catalog metadata.
217	23a. A native embedded-provider harness with configured provider sources must
218	     not synthesize a providerless fallback candidate when every live provider
219	     probe fails or returns no models. It must surface no eligible provider
220	     candidates with rejection evidence instead.
221	24. The CLI exposes the joined inventory through `fiz --list-models`,
222	    with JSON support. Rows include model, harness, provider, endpoint/host,
223	    server instance, power, provider/deployment class, cost, speed/perf signal,
224	    maximum configured context length, context source,
225	    availability, catalog reference, auto-routable status, and exact-pin-only
226	    status.
227	25. Routing filters candidates by hard caller constraints first:
228	    - `Model` means only that model identity may be used.
229	    - `Provider` means only that provider source/type or explicit endpoint
230	      selector may be used, depending on the request surface.
231	    - `Harness` means only that harness may be used.
232	26. `Profile`, `MinPower`, and `MaxPower` filter only unpinned automatic
233	    routing. A profile expands to an effective power policy before candidate
234	    filtering. Numeric bounds supplied with a profile further constrain that
235	    policy. None of these fields widen or override hard model/provider/harness
236	    pins.
237	27. When no `MinPower` or `MaxPower` is supplied, automatic routing still uses
238	    the discovered inventory and selects the best lowest-cost viable
239	    auto-routable model according to power, cost, availability, speed, context,
240	    and capability.
241	28. Automatic routing excludes inactive, deprecated, exact-pin-only, and
242	    unknown-power models unless the caller explicitly pins that model and live
243	    discovery confirms it is available.
244	29. The router ranks survivors by model power, provider/deployment placement,
245	    effective marginal cost, prepaid quota, availability, maximum configured
246	    context length, context/capability fit, observed speed/latency, normalized
247	    utilization, and sticky server-instance affinity.
248	30. When unpinned local/free LLMs are available and satisfy requested power,
249	    tools, context, and health constraints, they are preferred over paid cloud
250	    candidates. This local/free preference never overrides hard pins,
251	    `MinPower`/`MaxPower`, or capability requirements.
252	30a. For multiple eligible local/free server instances, routing assigns each
253	     new sticky route key to the least-loaded eligible server instance. Load
254	     combines service-owned in-flight route leases with fresh provider-owned
255	     utilization probes when available. Requests with the same sticky route key
256	     receive a ranking bonus for that server instance so worker-local cache
257	     behavior stays stable across related requests, including requests that use
258	     a different model on the same server.
259	30b. Sticky affinity never bypasses eligibility. A sticky server instance may
260	     lose when it no longer satisfies hard pins, power policy, context,
261	     capability, health, quota, or hard saturation constraints. A merely better
262	     score on another server instance is not enough to move an existing sticky
263	     key; severe utilization or performance pressure is enough when the scoring
264	     policy says the affinity bonus is outweighed.
265	30c. On a single machine, in-process route leases provide the authoritative
266	     sticky assignment and fallback load count. On multiple machines, correct
267	     cross-process stickiness and fair distribution require a shared lease
268	     backend; server metrics are advisory and racy, not a replacement for
269	     shared leases. See
270	     [plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md](../../02-design/plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md)
271	     for the lease-record and atomic acquire/refresh/release contract.
272	30d. Local provider utilization is provider-owned and type-derived where the
273	     server exposes it. `vllm` uses root `/metrics`. `llama-server` uses root
274	     `/metrics` when started with `--metrics` and root `/slots` as fallback.
275	     `omlx` uses root `/api/status` and may optionally consume admin-only
276	     `/admin/api/stats` when explicitly configured. `rapid-mlx` uses its
277	     documented status or metrics surface when available and otherwise reports
278	     unknown utilization with service-owned lease fallback. A configured
279	     OpenAI-compatible `base_url` ending in `/v1` is converted to the server
280	     root for these probes. Ollama's documented native surfaces expose request
281	     timing on `POST /api/chat` or `POST /api/generate` via
282	     `total_duration`, `load_duration`, `prompt_eval_count`,
283	     `prompt_eval_duration`, `eval_count`, and `eval_duration`; loaded-model
284	     inventory and allocated `context_length` come from `GET /api/ps`.
285	     Ollama's native surfaces do not expose a verified cache-pressure counter,
286	     so cache remains unknown unless a future probe adds it. LM Studio
287	     currently has verified native chat performance and model-management
288	     surfaces, but no live utilization probe, so it stays on the
289	     unknown/service-owned fallback path until a follow-up probe bead lands.
290	31. `agent.Run()` still receives one concrete `Provider` per attempt. `Execute`
291	    selects and dispatches the top candidate once.
292	32. The selected concrete harness, provider source, endpoint, model, requested
293	    model input, resolved model reference, profile, effective power policy,
294	    server instance, maximum configured context length, sticky assignment
295	    status, endpoint utilization source/freshness, performance signal, and
296	    score components are recorded in the result/session artifacts when known.
297	33. Existing `backends`, `default_backend`, `--backend`, and user-authored
298	    route-table surfaces are deprecated compatibility inputs during migration
299	    and must emit warnings if still parsed.
300	
301	#### Phase 2B (P1): Availability Feedback Without Agent Retry
302	
303	34. Fizeau may track recent provider/endpoint/model availability failures
304	    and temporarily back off unhealthy candidates using a bounded cooldown
305	    window.
306	35. Availability feedback is keyed at least by `(harness, provider source,
307	    endpoint, model)` so one bad endpoint or model does not poison a whole
308	    provider source, family, or power band.
309	36. `Execute` does not try a second candidate after dispatching the selected
310	    candidate. It returns attempted-route identity and failure class so callers
311	    can decide whether to issue a new request.
312	37. Prompt-shape, tool-schema, semantic task failures, test failures, review
313	    blocks, or low-quality output do not trigger agent-owned retry. Those are
314	    caller-owned retry/escalation signals.
315	38. Callers continue to pass model intent (`MinPower`, `MaxPower`, `model_ref`,
316	    or exact pin) into the embedded harness. Callers must not duplicate inner
317	    provider-selection logic.
318	
319	#### Phase 2C (P1): Placement and Quota-Aware Scoring
320	
321	39. Placement and `surface_policy` catalog data may carry placement order, cost
322	    ceilings, failure policy, and reasoning defaults. These fields refine
323	    scoring and filtering within the numeric power/pin constraints.
324	40. The routing engine uses live quota signals to influence subscription candidate scoring:
325	    - `QuotaOK` — false when a subscription provider is exhausted.
326	    - `QuotaPercentUsed` — known usage percentage; applies a penalty when high (>= 80%).
327	    - `QuotaStale` — applies a penalty when the latest quota probe is older than the configured freshness window.
328	    - `QuotaTrend` — biases score based on burn rate (`healthy`, `burning`, `exhausting`).
329	41. Quota and placement signals only affect ranking and filtering within the
330	    eligible candidate set that satisfies requested power bounds and hard pins.
331	    They do not trigger automatic semantic escalation.
332	
333	### Non-Functional Requirements
334	
335	- **Simplicity**: library users can still pass a concrete `agent.Provider`
336	  directly with no YAML, catalog, or routing machinery.
337	- **Clarity**: prompt presets, provider config, model policy, and provider
338	  routing each use distinct terminology.
339	- **Boundary safety**: Callers may depend on agent-owned routing for the embedded
340	  harness, but they express power bounds and hard pins rather than reproducing
341	  provider candidate logic.
342	- **Updateability**: rapidly changing model policy/data can be refreshed via an
343	  external manifest without requiring every consumer to wait for a new Go
344	  release.
345	- **Compatibility**: legacy configured endpoint names and route-table inputs,
346	  when present, are migration-only and not the target architecture.
347	
348	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
349	
350	- **Unknown provider source or endpoint selector**: route resolution returns an
351	  error before dispatch.
352	- **Unknown model reference**: catalog resolution returns an error before the
353	  run.
354	- **Unsatisfied exact model/provider-source/endpoint/harness pin**: route
355	  resolution returns a no-candidate error with rejected candidates and reasons;
356	  it does not choose a broader model, source, endpoint, or harness.
357	- **Unknown or missing-power model**: excluded from unpinned automatic routing;
358	  exact pins may use it when live discovery confirms availability.
359	- **Deprecated or stale model reference**: resolution returns metadata that the
360	  caller may surface as a warning or block according to policy.
361	- **Manifest missing or unreadable**: fall back to the embedded snapshot unless
362	  the caller explicitly required the external manifest.
363	- **Selected provider not reachable**:
364	  return an attempted-route error containing harness, provider source,
365	  endpoint, model, and failure class. The agent does not try another candidate
366	  in that request.
367	- **Utilization probe unavailable or stale**: keep the endpoint eligible if
368	  normal model discovery and health checks pass. Use service-owned route leases
369	  as the load signal and mark utilization source/freshness as unknown or stale
370	  in route evidence.
371	- **Sticky server instance unavailable or ineligible**: invalidate or demote
372	  that sticky assignment and resolve from the currently eligible candidate set.
373	  Record the reason.
374	- **Semantic task failure**: caller-owned. DDx or another caller may retry with
375	  a stronger `MinPower`, capped `MaxPower`, or different pins, but the agent
376	  does not infer semantic failure or escalate automatically.
377

8	# Feature Specification: FEAT-004 — Shared Model Catalog, Power-Based Routing, and Provider Configuration
9	
10	**Feature ID**: FEAT-004
11	**Status**: Draft
12	**Priority**: P0 (provider sources/endpoints), P1 (shared catalog), P1 (power-based routing)
13	**Owner**: Fizeau Team
14	
15	## Overview
16	
17	Fizeau keeps the runtime boundary deliberately simple: `agent.Run()` receives
18	one resolved `Provider`. Configuration declares provider sources and endpoints;
19	it does not contain complicated route rules. The agent discovers what models
20	those sources can serve, joins that inventory with catalog power/cost/speed
21	metadata, tracks usage and availability, and automatically routes to the best
22	candidate that satisfies the requested power and hard constraints. If the
23	caller supplies no power bounds, the agent selects the best lowest-cost viable
24	auto-routable model from the discovered inventory.
25	
26	This feature therefore has three related but separate responsibilities:
27	
28	- **Provider sources and endpoints** — concrete transport/auth definitions for
29	  provider types such as `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `vllm`, `llama-server`,
30	  `openrouter`, `anthropic`, and subprocess harnesses such as `codex` or
31	  `claude`
32	- **Shared model catalog** — agent-owned model metadata, numeric power,
33	  aliases, surface mappings, deprecations, costs, and benchmark provenance
34	- **Power-based routing** — generated candidate inventory plus deterministic
35	  selection within caller-supplied hard constraints and optional power bounds
36	
37	Prompt presets stay separate from all three. `preset` already means system
38	prompt behavior and must not be reused for model policy or routing.
39	
40	## Terminology
41	
42	- **Provider source** — the implementation/source type used to reach models,
43	  such as `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `ollama`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `codex`, or
44	  `claude`
45	- **Endpoint** — a concrete configured transport/auth location for a provider
46	  source: base URL, headers/credentials, optional host label, and optional
47	  default model hint. Endpoint identity is diagnostic and filterable; it is not
48	  the primary routing abstraction.
49	- **Model catalog** — agent-owned policy/data describing model families,
50	  numeric power, aliases, canonical policy targets, provider/deployment class,
51	  deprecation/staleness status, costs, benchmark inputs, and surface mappings
52	- **Manifest** — the structured model-catalog data file maintained separately
53	  from Go logic and consumed by the catalog package
54	- **Model reference** — a user-facing name resolved through the catalog, such
55	  as a concrete model entry or optional alias
56	- **Profile** — a named shorthand for a power-policy point or bounded power
57	  range, with optional ranking preferences. Profiles do not name a closed set
58	  of concrete models and do not override hard pins.
59	- **Canonical target** — the stable policy target the catalog wants a given
60	  reference to resolve to; one target may project to different concrete models
61	  and reasoning defaults on different consumer surfaces
62	- **Power** — an integer model-strength score from 1 to 10. Higher means more
63	  capable for agent tasks. `0` means unknown, missing, or not eligible for
64	  automatic routing.
65	- **Provider/deployment class** — catalog provenance describing whether a model
66	  is a managed cloud frontier model, prepaid harness model, metered API model,
67	  local/free inference server, community/self-hosted copy, or test model.
68	  Benchmarks alone do not make different deployment classes equivalent.
69	- **Route candidate** — one discovered `(harness, provider source, endpoint,
70	  model)` option after joining live inventory with catalog metadata
71	- **Server instance** — the concrete inference server reached by a candidate,
72	  derived from endpoint configuration or normalized host/port, such as
73	  `grendel`, `vidar`, or `sindri`. Stickiness targets server instances, not
74	  model strings.
75	- **Sticky route key** — a request sequence identity, normally the validated
76	  `CorrelationID` or a future worker/session sequence ID, used to bias related
77	  requests toward the same server instance
78	- **Endpoint utilization** — a normalized operational signal for one provider
79	  endpoint, including active requests, queued/deferred requests, concurrency
80	  when known, cache pressure when known, freshness, and source
81	- **Prompt preset** — system prompt selection (`preset`, `--preset`); unrelated
82	  to model policy and routing
83	
84	## Problem Statement
85	
86	- **Current situation**: Fizeau can select configured transport endpoints
87	  directly, while callers and orchestrators still carry duplicated or
88	  mismatched routing assumptions above it.
89	- **Pain points**: Prompt presets already occupy the `preset` naming surface,
90	  provider configs currently mix transport and model concerns, and route tables
91	  force operators to encode policy that the agent can derive from live model
92	  inventory and the catalog.
93	- **Desired outcome**: Fizeau becomes the reusable source of truth for model
94	  aliases, numeric power, deprecations, deployment-class-aware model metadata,
95	  and embedded provider selection, while callers keep retry/escalation policy
96	  and HELIX keeps stage intent only.
97	
98	## Requirements
99	
100	### Functional Requirements
101	
102	#### Phase 1 (P0): Provider Sources and Endpoints
103	
104	1. `Config` specifies provider sources with concrete `type` values (`openai`,
105	   `openrouter`, `lmstudio`, `omlx`, `vllm`, `llama-server`, `ollama`,
106	   `anthropic`, and harness-backed sources where applicable) plus endpoint
107	   transport/auth data such as base URL, API key, headers, and optional
108	   endpoint pools. `type: openai-compat` is rejected at config load; use the
109	   actual model source instead.
110	2. Endpoint labels may exist for diagnostics, host display, and explicit
111	   endpoint selection, but stable user-authored endpoint labels are not the
112	   primary routing API.
113	3. A provider endpoint may carry a default model hint for direct dispatch, but
114	   endpoint config is not the canonical source of model aliases, power, or
115	   routing policy.
116	4. The CLI can constrain routing by provider source/type and, when necessary,
117	   by a concrete endpoint selector. Source/type constraints are preferred over
118	   arbitrary configured endpoint labels.
119	5. If a caller selects one exact endpoint, all requests go to that endpoint. If
120	   it fails, the request fails with attempted-route evidence.
121	6. No retry across endpoints or sources happens inside one agent request.
122	   Provider SDK retries within one endpoint remain governed by FEAT-003.
123	7. The harness, provider source, endpoint identity, and model used are recorded
124	   in the `Result`.
125	
126	#### Phase 1B (P1): Shared Model Catalog and Manifest
127	
128	7. Fizeau owns a reusable shared model catalog separate from provider configs
129	   and prompt presets.
130	8. The catalog represents:
131	   - model families
132	   - numeric power on a 1..10 scale, with `0` reserved for unknown or
133	     exact-pin-only models
134	   - optional model aliases for exact model identity and migration
135	   - canonical policy targets
136	   - per-model entries for every concrete model eligible for a tier
137	   - ordered tier candidate lists that can contain multiple concrete models
138	   - deprecated or stale targets with replacement metadata
139	   - provider/deployment class and provenance for power assignment
140	   - consumer-surface mappings where a canonical target needs different
141	     concrete strings and may carry different reasoning defaults for different
142	     downstream integrations
143	   - provider-specific concrete surface IDs on model entries, so a single tier
144	     can choose among Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible, Codex, or Claude Code model
145	     strings without duplicating cost and benchmark metadata
146	   - per-model reasoning capability metadata, including supported named values,
147	     numeric maximums, and named-to-token maps when a provider/model cannot
148	     derive safe limits from live metadata
149	9. Catalog data is stored in a structured manifest maintained separately from
150	   Go logic inside the agent repo.
151	10. Fizeau ships an embedded snapshot of that manifest and may also load an
152	    external manifest override so policy/data can update independently of code
153	    releases where practical.
154	11. Fizeau publishes versioned catalog manifests outside normal binary
155	    releases and exposes a stable machine-readable channel pointer so operators
156	    and callers can refresh policy more quickly than the binary release cadence.
157	12. Catalog refresh is explicit. Ordinary request execution must not fetch
158	    remote manifest data.
159	13. The Fizeau CLI and any caller can resolve a model reference through the
160	    catalog to a concrete model string appropriate for the chosen consumer
161	    surface.
162	13a. When a profile or canonical target has an ordered candidate list,
163	     provider-backed routing tests those candidates against the endpoint's
164	     live model inventory in order. The router chooses the first candidate the
165	     endpoint advertises instead of failing only because the target's primary
166	     candidate is absent.
167	13b. Provider-native model names may include vendor prefixes, casing,
168	     quantization, accelerator, or packaging suffixes such as
169	     `Qwen3.6-27B-MLX-8bit`. Catalog metadata lookup must match those names
170	     back to the intended catalog model when the canonical identity is
171	     unambiguous, so auto-routing sees the catalog power, context window, tool
172	     support, and auto-routable status for the selected provider-native ID.
173	14. Explicit concrete model pins remain supported as hard constraints. If the
174	    requested model is unavailable, routing fails with detailed evidence rather
175	    than substituting another model.
176	15. Ownership split is explicit:
177	    - agent owns model catalog data/policy and provider-source/endpoint
178	      selection inside the embedded runtime
179	    - callers own cross-harness orchestration, semantic retry, and guardrails
180	    - HELIX owns stage intent only
181	16. The catalog uses `reasoning_default` for model-reasoning policy.
182	17. `reasoning_default` is a single scalar using the same value grammar as the
183	    public CLI/config/API `reasoning` field: `auto`, `off`, `low`, `medium`,
184	    `high`, supported extended values such as `minimal`, `xhigh` / `x-high`,
185	    and `max`, or numeric values such as `0`, `2048`, and `8192`.
186	18. Catalog defaults are keyed to model metadata and numeric power. Profiles
187	    are allowed only as named shorthands for specific points on the power curve
188	    or bounded power-policy ranges. They are not routing personas and do not
189	    resolve to a closed list of models.
190	    - Explicit caller `reasoning` always wins over tier defaults, including
191	      supported requests above high such as `xhigh`, `x-high`, or `max`, and
192	      explicit numeric values.
193	19. Catalog candidates for numeric-only reasoning providers must publish
194	    per-model maximums or named-value maps unless the provider can derive safe
195	    limits from live metadata. The router must fail clearly on explicit
196	    unsupported or over-limit requests and may drop only auto/default reasoning
197	    controls for unsupported candidates.
198	20. Manifest schema v4 stores cost, context, benchmark, OpenRouter ID, and
199	    surface model strings on top-level `models` entries. Target entries retain
200	    tier policy only: family, aliases, status/replacement metadata,
201	    `context_window_min`, `swe_bench_min`, ordered `candidates`, and
202	    `surface_policy`.
203	21. Catalog power synthesis uses benchmark inputs when available, but
204	    benchmark numbers are not sufficient on their own. Cost, recency,
205	    capability metadata, provider/deployment class, and explicit override
206	    reason all contribute to power. A local/community/self-hosted copy such as
207	    `gpt-oss-120b` or `minimax2.7` must not receive the same power as a managed
208	    cloud frontier Sonnet/Opus/GPT model solely because one benchmark is high.
209	22. Models with missing or zero power remain inspectable and may be used by
210	    exact pin when available, but are excluded from unpinned automatic routing.
211	
212	#### Phase 2A (P1): Candidate Inventory and Power-Based Routing
213	
214	23. Fizeau builds the candidate set by enumerating available harnesses,
215	    provider sources, endpoints, and discovered model IDs, then joining that
216	    live inventory with catalog metadata.
217	23a. A native embedded-provider harness with configured provider sources must
218	     not synthesize a providerless fallback candidate when every live provider
219	     probe fails or returns no models. It must surface no eligible provider
220	     candidates with rejection evidence instead.
221	24. The CLI exposes the joined inventory through `fiz --list-models`,
222	    with JSON support. Rows include model, harness, provider, endpoint/host,
223	    server instance, power, provider/deployment class, cost, speed/perf signal,
224	    maximum configured context length, context source,
225	    availability, catalog reference, auto-routable status, and exact-pin-only
226	    status.
227	25. Routing filters candidates by hard caller constraints first:
228	    - `Model` means only that model identity may be used.
229	    - `Provider` means only that provider source/type or explicit endpoint
230	      selector may be used, depending on the request surface.
231	    - `Harness` means only that harness may be used.
232	26. `Profile`, `MinPower`, and `MaxPower` filter only unpinned automatic
233	    routing. A profile expands to an effective power policy before candidate
234	    filtering. Numeric bounds supplied with a profile further constrain that
235	    policy. None of these fields widen or override hard model/provider/harness
236	    pins.
237	27. When no `MinPower` or `MaxPower` is supplied, automatic routing still uses
238	    the discovered inventory and selects the best lowest-cost viable
239	    auto-routable model according to power, cost, availability, speed, context,
240	    and capability.
241	28. Automatic routing excludes inactive, deprecated, exact-pin-only, and
242	    unknown-power models unless the caller explicitly pins that model and live
243	    discovery confirms it is available.
244	29. The router ranks survivors by model power, provider/deployment placement,
245	    effective marginal cost, prepaid quota, availability, maximum configured
246	    context length, context/capability fit, observed speed/latency, normalized
247	    utilization, and sticky server-instance affinity.
248	30. When unpinned local/free LLMs are available and satisfy requested power,
249	    tools, context, and health constraints, they are preferred over paid cloud
250	    candidates. This local/free preference never overrides hard pins,
251	    `MinPower`/`MaxPower`, or capability requirements.
252	30a. For multiple eligible local/free server instances, routing assigns each
253	     new sticky route key to the least-loaded eligible server instance. Load
254	     combines service-owned in-flight route leases with fresh provider-owned
255	     utilization probes when available. Requests with the same sticky route key
256	     receive a ranking bonus for that server instance so worker-local cache
257	     behavior stays stable across related requests, including requests that use
258	     a different model on the same server.
259	30b. Sticky affinity never bypasses eligibility. A sticky server instance may
260	     lose when it no longer satisfies hard pins, power policy, context,
261	     capability, health, quota, or hard saturation constraints. A merely better
262	     score on another server instance is not enough to move an existing sticky
263	     key; severe utilization or performance pressure is enough when the scoring
264	     policy says the affinity bonus is outweighed.
265	30c. On a single machine, in-process route leases provide the authoritative
266	     sticky assignment and fallback load count. On multiple machines, correct
267	     cross-process stickiness and fair distribution require a shared lease
268	     backend; server metrics are advisory and racy, not a replacement for
269	     shared leases. See
270	     [plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md](../../02-design/plan-2026-05-05-shared-lease-backend.md)
271	     for the lease-record and atomic acquire/refresh/release contract.
272	30d. Local provider utilization is provider-owned and type-derived where the
273	     server exposes it. `vllm` uses root `/metrics`. `llama-server` uses root
274	     `/metrics` when started with `--metrics` and root `/slots` as fallback.
275	     `omlx` uses root `/api/status` and may optionally consume admin-only
276	     `/admin/api/stats` when explicitly configured. `rapid-mlx` uses its
277	     documented status or metrics surface when available and otherwise reports
278	     unknown utilization with service-owned lease fallback. A configured
279	     OpenAI-compatible `base_url` ending in `/v1` is converted to the server
280	     root for these probes. Ollama's documented native surfaces expose request
281	     timing on `POST /api/chat` or `POST /api/generate` via
282	     `total_duration`, `load_duration`, `prompt_eval_count`,
283	     `prompt_eval_duration`, `eval_count`, and `eval_duration`; loaded-model
284	     inventory and allocated `context_length` come from `GET /api/ps`.
285	     Ollama's native surfaces do not expose a verified cache-pressure counter,
286	     so cache remains unknown unless a future probe adds it. LM Studio
287	     currently has verified native chat performance and model-management
288	     surfaces, but no live utilization probe, so it stays on the
289	     unknown/service-owned fallback path until a follow-up probe bead lands.
290	31. `agent.Run()` still receives one concrete `Provider` per attempt. `Execute`
291	    selects and dispatches the top candidate once.
292	32. The selected concrete harness, provider source, endpoint, model, requested
293	    model input, resolved model reference, profile, effective power policy,
294	    server instance, maximum configured context length, sticky assignment
295	    status, endpoint utilization source/freshness, performance signal, and
296	    score components are recorded in the result/session artifacts when known.
297	33. Existing `backends`, `default_backend`, `--backend`, and user-authored
298	    route-table surfaces are deprecated compatibility inputs during migration
299	    and must emit warnings if still parsed.
300	
301	#### Phase 2B (P1): Availability Feedback Without Agent Retry
302	
303	34. Fizeau may track recent provider/endpoint/model availability failures
304	    and temporarily back off unhealthy candidates using a bounded cooldown
305	    window.
306	35. Availability feedback is keyed at least by `(harness, provider source,
307	    endpoint, model)` so one bad endpoint or model does not poison a whole
308	    provider source, family, or power band.
309	36. `Execute` does not try a second candidate after dispatching the selected
310	    candidate. It returns attempted-route identity and failure class so callers
311	    can decide whether to issue a new request.
312	37. Prompt-shape, tool-schema, semantic task failures, test failures, review
313	    blocks, or low-quality output do not trigger agent-owned retry. Those are
314	    caller-owned retry/escalation signals.
315	38. Callers continue to pass model intent (`MinPower`, `MaxPower`, `model_ref`,
316	    or exact pin) into the embedded harness. Callers must not duplicate inner
317	    provider-selection logic.
318	
319	#### Phase 2C (P1): Placement and Quota-Aware Scoring
320	
321	39. Placement and `surface_policy` catalog data may carry placement order, cost
322	    ceilings, failure policy, and reasoning defaults. These fields refine
323	    scoring and filtering within the numeric power/pin constraints.
324	40. The routing engine uses live quota signals to influence subscription candidate scoring:
325	    - `QuotaOK` — false when a subscription provider is exhausted.
326	    - `QuotaPercentUsed` — known usage percentage; applies a penalty when high (>= 80%).
327	    - `QuotaStale` — applies a penalty when the latest quota probe is older than the configured freshness window.
328	    - `QuotaTrend` — biases score based on burn rate (`healthy`, `burning`, `exhausting`).
329	41. Quota and placement signals only affect ranking and filtering within the
330	    eligible candidate set that satisfies requested power bounds and hard pins.
331	    They do not trigger automatic semantic escalation.
332	
333	### Non-Functional Requirements
334	
335	- **Simplicity**: library users can still pass a concrete `agent.Provider`
336	  directly with no YAML, catalog, or routing machinery.
337	- **Clarity**: prompt presets, provider config, model policy, and provider
338	  routing each use distinct terminology.
339	- **Boundary safety**: Callers may depend on agent-owned routing for the embedded
340	  harness, but they express power bounds and hard pins rather than reproducing
341	  provider candidate logic.
342	- **Updateability**: rapidly changing model policy/data can be refreshed via an
343	  external manifest without requiring every consumer to wait for a new Go
344	  release.
345	- **Compatibility**: legacy configured endpoint names and route-table inputs,
346	  when present, are migration-only and not the target architecture.
347	
348	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
349	
350	- **Unknown provider source or endpoint selector**: route resolution returns an
351	  error before dispatch.
352	- **Unknown model reference**: catalog resolution returns an error before the
353	  run.
354	- **Unsatisfied exact model/provider-source/endpoint/harness pin**: route
355	  resolution returns a no-candidate error with rejected candidates and reasons;
356	  it does not choose a broader model, source, endpoint, or harness.
357	- **Unknown or missing-power model**: excluded from unpinned automatic routing;
358	  exact pins may use it when live discovery confirms availability.
359	- **Deprecated or stale model reference**: resolution returns metadata that the
360	  caller may surface as a warning or block according to policy.
361	- **Manifest missing or unreadable**: fall back to the embedded snapshot unless
362	  the caller explicitly required the external manifest.
363	- **Selected provider not reachable**:
364	  return an attempted-route error containing harness, provider source,
365	  endpoint, model, and failure class. The agent does not try another candidate
366	  in that request.
367	- **Utilization probe unavailable or stale**: keep the endpoint eligible if
368	  normal model discovery and health checks pass. Use service-owned route leases
369	  as the load signal and mark utilization source/freshness as unknown or stale
370	  in route evidence.
371	- **Sticky server instance unavailable or ineligible**: invalidate or demote
372	  that sticky assignment and resolve from the currently eligible candidate set.
373	  Record the reason.
374	- **Semantic task failure**: caller-owned. DDx or another caller may retry with
375	  a stronger `MinPower`, capped `MaxPower`, or different pins, but the agent
376	  does not infer semantic failure or escalate automatically.
377	
378	## Success Metrics
379	
380	- Provider source/endpoint config works with LM Studio, Ollama, OpenRouter, and
381	  Anthropic without making arbitrary configured names the primary route
382	  primitive.
383	- Callers can consume agent-owned catalog data without maintaining duplicate alias
384	  and power tables.
385	- Operators can run `fiz --list-models` to inspect the same joined model
386	  inventory the router scores.
387	- Prompt preset docs and model-policy docs stay terminology-safe and do not
388	  overload `preset`.
389	- Power-based routing selects one candidate deterministically and records the
390	  actual harness/provider-source/endpoint/model used.
391	
392	## Acceptance Criteria
393	
394	| ID | Criterion | Suggested Verification |
395	|----|-----------|------------------------|
396	| AC-FEAT-004-01 | Provider source/endpoint resolution selects the configured transport before the run starts, and unknown provider source or endpoint selectors fail during config/CLI resolution rather than inside `agent.Run()`. | `go test ./internal/config ./cmd/fiz ./...` |
397	| AC-FEAT-004-02 | Model references resolve through the embedded or external manifest to the correct consumer-surface model string and per-surface reasoning metadata, and missing references/surfaces fail deterministically before the run. | `go test ./internal/modelcatalog ./internal/config ./cmd/fiz ./...` |
398	| AC-FEAT-004-03 | Deprecated or stale model references are rejected by default, surface replacement metadata, and can be explicitly allowed only when the caller opts in. | `go test ./internal/modelcatalog ./internal/config ./cmd/fiz ./...` |
399	| AC-FEAT-004-04 | An explicit concrete `--model`, provider-source/endpoint constraint, or `--harness` is a hard constraint.
